fixes: Natural style: the bed and banks read as a single folded tilted sheet (a crumpled wedge) with rocks sprinkled on top, not a rock-lined stream. Build real banks: two continuous rows of overlapping boulders 0.25-0.5 m high on each side, bed 0.1-0.2 m below the bank tops, and make the bed flat per weir step with a 0.1-0.17 m drop (sheet shows 0.17 m).

Stepped style (runnel beside stairs): currently stacked cubes with a staggered jumble and a floating gap beneath; concept side view is 4-5 ashlar steps, each 0.17 m drop and about 0.3 m tread, with water falling over each lip and masonry walls both sides. Rebuild as a staircase of treads with side walls 0.25 m thick and flush lips; remove the gaps and floating blocks.

Kerbed style: kerbs are huge flat slabs with untextured planar sides and the water is a sheet inside a box, plus a loose slab laid over the top. Concept has a cut-stone kerb 0.15-0.2 m wide, 0.3 m tall, with rock clusters at ends. Reduce kerb section to 0.18 x 0.3 m, add a bevel, joints every 0.6-0.9 m, and a few rock stones at the ends only.

Weirs: no distinct weir lips in any style. Add a visible lip (0.06 m projecting, 0.12 m drop) every n m and a plunge pool below with the next bed 0.1-0.17 m lower; lookbook 04 shows rock weirs with 3-4 thin falls across a 1.5 m width.

Scale and proportion: the natural canonical looks 2 m wide and bulky for a 4 m run; target width 0.3-2.5 m per the asset list and bank height at most 0.35 m so a person can step over. Add stepping stones in the bed (library stepping_stone is listed but not visible).

LOD2/LOD3: at 35 m and 80 m the model is a thin dark V. Seeds change style, so the proxies are completely different shapes; keep the water strip as a lighter band and the banks as two thin parallel strips so it reads as a stream. LOD3 seed 2 is 10 tris and invisible. Raise LOD3 to the 20 tri budget with both banks.
library_issues: basalt_wet reads as bright foil on the kerbs and slab faces.
paving on the kerbed style is untextured pale grey with hard shading edges.
water_river is a flat cyan plane: fine as a runtime-fx placeholder.
summary: The weakest of the three. The three styles vary strongly, but none reads like the concept's rock-lined stream with small weirs, the cut-stone rill, or the stepped runnel. Natural is a folded sheet, kerbed a set of plain slabs, stepped a pile of cubes. LOD2/3 are specks.
